# 2D contour

Type id `contour_2d` · category: 2-D · runs in Setups of kind: three_axis, indexed

Cuts along a curve, or around the walls of a part, at one or more depths. It can add finishing passes and holding tabs, so it is the usual way to cut out a part. A finishing type.

- Takes the material it cuts out of the stock for the toolpaths after it: yes.

See [Add a toolpath](Add-a-Toolpath) for how to add one, and the [list of toolpath types](Toolpath-Types).

In the project file a setting is written as `group.key`, for example `passes.stepover`. In the app the inspector shows each group on its own tab. Lengths are in millimetres in the file whatever unit the project shows.

## Tool

| Setting | File key | Value | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Spindle speed | `tool_params.spindle_rpm` | rev/min | from the tool's cutting data (`rpm`) | How fast the spindle turns. Left empty, it comes from the tool's cutting data for the Setup's material. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: tool, Setup material. |
| Feed | `tool_params.feed` | group of settings (below) |  |  |
| Cut feed | `tool_params.feed.cut` | mm/min | from the tool's cutting data (`feed`) | How fast the tool moves while it cuts. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: tool, Setup material. |
| Plunge feed | `tool_params.feed.plunge` | mm/min | from the tool's cutting data (`plunge`) | How fast the tool moves straight down into the material. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: tool, Setup material. |
| Ramp | `tool_params.feed.ramp` | mm/min | calculated from feed.cut | Feed while the tool ramps into the material. Left empty, it is the cut feed. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: `feed.cut`. |
| Lead in | `tool_params.feed.lead_in` | mm/min | calculated from feed.cut | Feed on the lead-in move. Left empty, it is the cut feed. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: `feed.cut`. |
| Lead out | `tool_params.feed.lead_out` | mm/min | calculated from feed.lead_in | Feed on the lead-out move. Left empty, it is the lead-in feed. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: `feed.lead_in`. |
| Transition | `tool_params.feed.transition` | mm/min | calculated from feed.cut | Feed on the short moves that link one pass to the next while the tool stays down. Left empty, it is the cut feed. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: `feed.cut`. |
| Coolant | `tool_params.coolant` | `off`, `flood`, `mist` | `off` | Coolant to switch on for this toolpath. The post must have a coolant block, or you get a warning. Depends on: post `coolant_on` event. |

## Geometry

| Setting | File key | Value | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Drive faces | `geometry.drive_faces` | selection of bodies, faces or edges | not set | The faces this toolpath machines. 3-D types machine every face of the Setup's bodies when this is empty; 2-D types need something selected. Allowed: faces of the Setup's bodies. Depends on: Setup `geometry`. |
| Drive curves | `geometry.drive_curves` | selection of bodies, faces or edges | not set | The curves this toolpath follows or fills. 2-D types need curves or faces. The app cannot pick curves yet; set them in the project file. Allowed: edges, wire curves, planar faces. Depends on: Setup `geometry`. |
| Excluded faces | `geometry.excluded_faces` | selection of bodies, faces or edges | not set | Faces to leave out: the tool is allowed to cut into them. |

## Heights

A height is a reference plus an offset in mm, for example `{ ref = "stock_top", offset = 5 }`. The reference is one of `setup_clearance`, `stock_top`, `stock_bottom`, `model_top`, `model_bottom`, `work_zero`, `selection`.

| Setting | File key | Value | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clearance | `heights.clearance` | height: a `ref` and an `offset` in mm | `setup_clearance` | The height the tool rises to for the longest moves, above everything including clamps. Allowed: ≥ `retract`. Depends on: Setup clearance. |
| Retract | `heights.retract` | height: a `ref` and an `offset` in mm | `stock_top` + 5 | The height the tool rises to between cuts. It must not be below the feed height. Allowed: ≥ `feed`. Depends on: stock. |
| Feed | `heights.feed` | height: a `ref` and an `offset` in mm | `top` + 2 | The height where the tool changes from rapid to cutting feed on its way down. It is measured from the top height. Allowed: ≥ `top`. Depends on: `top`. |
| Top | `heights.top` | height: a `ref` and an `offset` in mm | `stock_top` | The top of the material this toolpath cuts. The first cut starts here. Allowed: > `bottom` (≥ for `parallel`). Depends on: per type. |
| Bottom | `heights.bottom` | height: a `ref` and an `offset` in mm | `selection` | The bottom of the cut: the lowest point the tool reaches. Depends on: per type. |

## Passes

| Setting | File key | Value | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Machining tolerance | `passes.machining_tolerance` | mm | 0.01 | How far the calculated path may stray from the ideal path. A smaller number gives a smoother path and a longer program. Allowed: ≥ 1e-4. |
| Max segment length | `passes.max_segment_length` | mm | not set | Longest straight move in the path. Left empty, there is no limit. Allowed: > 0. |
| Output arcs | `passes.output_arcs` | yes or no | yes | Write arcs as arc moves (G2 and G3) where the path has them. Off writes only straight moves. Depends on: post arc support. |
| Side | `passes.side` | `inside`, `outside`, `left`, `right`, `on` | calculated from outside (closed chains) or right (open chains) | Which side of the curve the tool cuts on: `inside` or `outside` for closed curves, `left` or `right` for open ones, or `on` to put the tool centre on the curve. Allowed: `inside`/`outside` closed chains only; `left`/`right` open chains only. Depends on: chain closure. |
| Direction | `passes.direction` | `climb`, `conventional` | `climb` | Which way the tool travels. `climb` has the material on the right of the tool as it moves (with a clockwise spindle), `conventional` the opposite. `zigzag` alternates direction on every pass, and `any`, `selection` and `reversed` follow the curves as selected. Depends on: `side` ≠ `on`. |
| Compensation | `passes.compensation` | `computer`, `control`, `wear` | `computer` | `computer` puts the tool radius into the path. `control` leaves it to the machine's cutter compensation (G41, G42), so the post must support it. `wear` does both, so the operator can adjust for wear. Depends on: `side`, post. |
| Step down | `passes.step_down` | mm | from the tool's cutting data (`step_down`) | How deep each level cuts. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: tool, material. |
| Depth count | `passes.depth_count` | count | not set | Cut this many equal levels instead of using a step-down. Set one or the other. Allowed: ≥ 1. Depends on: replaces `step_down`. |
| Finishing pass count | `passes.finishing_pass_count` | count | 0 | How many light finishing passes to run after the main cut. Allowed: 0 … 10 †. |
| Finishing stepover | `passes.finishing_stepover` | mm | calculated from 0.1 * tool.diameter | Distance between finishing passes. Left empty, a tenth of the tool diameter. Allowed: (0, D]. Depends on: `finishing_pass_count` > 0. |
| Finish every level | `passes.finish_every_level` | yes or no | no | Run the finishing passes at every level, not only at the last one. Depends on: `finishing_pass_count` > 0. |
| Spring pass count | `passes.spring_pass_count` | count | 0 | How many times to repeat the last pass unchanged, to take out the spring of the tool. Allowed: 0 … 5 †. |
| Stock to leave | `passes.stock_to_leave` | mm | 0 | Material left on the walls for a later finishing pass. A negative value cuts past the model, which is useful for inlays. Allowed: 2-D types: > −R; 3-D types: > −r (corner radius; ≥ 0 for flat tools) (§7, decision 3). Depends on: tool. |
| Stock to leave axial | `passes.stock_to_leave_axial` | mm | calculated from stock_to_leave | Material left on floors. Left empty, the same as the wall value. Allowed: ≥ 0. Depends on: `stock_to_leave`. |
| Start point | `passes.start_point` | point `[x, y, z]` in mm | not set | Where closed curves start. Left empty, the point nearest the end of the previous cut. Depends on: closed chains. |
| Tabs | `passes.tabs` | group of settings (below) |  |  |
| Mode | `passes.tabs.mode` | `off`, `count`, `distance`, `points` | `off` | Leave small bridges of material (tabs) so a cut-out part does not move: `off`, a `count` of them, one every `distance`, or at chosen `points`. |
| Count | `passes.tabs.count` | count | 4 | Number of tabs, spread evenly along the curve. Allowed: ≥ 1. Depends on: `tabs.mode` = `count`. |
| Distance | `passes.tabs.distance` | mm | 100 | Distance between tabs along the curve. Allowed: > `tabs.width`. Depends on: `tabs.mode` = `distance`. |
| Points | `passes.tabs.points` | list of points in mm | not set | Positions of the tabs. Allowed: ≥ 1 point. Depends on: `tabs.mode` = `points`. |
| Width | `passes.tabs.width` | mm | calculated from tool.diameter | Width of each tab. Left empty, the tool diameter. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: `tabs.mode` ≠ `off`. |
| Height | `passes.tabs.height` | mm | 1 | Height of each tab above the bottom of the cut. Allowed: (0, top − bottom]. Depends on: heights. |
| Ramp angle | `passes.tabs.ramp_angle_deg` | degrees | 45 | The angle the path rises over a tab at. Allowed: (0, 90]. Depends on: `tabs.mode` ≠ `off`. |

## Linking

| Setting | File key | Value | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Retract | `linking.retract` | `full`, `minimum`, `stay_down` | `minimum` | How the tool moves between passes: `full` always lifts to the retract height, `minimum` lifts only as far as needed, `stay_down` keeps the tool in the material when the straight move is clear. |
| Safety distance | `linking.safety_distance` | mm | 1 | How far above the highest point on the way the tool lifts when it retracts the minimum amount. Allowed: ≥ 0. Depends on: `retract` = `minimum`. |
| Transitions | `linking.transitions` | `direct`, `smooth` | `direct` | Whether the short moves between passes go straight or are smoothed. Depends on: `retract` ≠ `full`. |
| Lead in | `linking.lead_in` | group of settings (below) |  |  |
| Kind | `linking.lead_in.kind` | `none`, `arc`, `linear` | `arc` | How the tool eases into the cut: not at all, along a quarter circle, or along a straight line. |
| Radius | `linking.lead_in.radius` | mm | calculated from 0.5 * tool.diameter | Radius of an arc lead-in. Left empty, half the tool diameter. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: `lead_in.kind` = `arc`. |
| Length | `linking.lead_in.length` | mm | calculated from 0 (arc) or tool.radius (linear) | Length of the straight part of the lead-in. Allowed: ≥ 0. Depends on: `lead_in.kind`. |
| Lead out | `linking.lead_out` | group of settings (below) |  | Depends on: `lead_in`. |
| Kind | `linking.lead_out.kind` | `none`, `arc`, `linear` | `arc` | How the tool eases out of the cut. Left empty, the same as the lead-in. |
| Radius | `linking.lead_out.radius` | mm | calculated from 0.5 * tool.diameter | Radius of an arc lead-out. |
| Length | `linking.lead_out.length` | mm | calculated from 0 (arc) or tool.radius (linear) | Length of the straight part of the lead-out. |
| Ramp | `linking.ramp` | group of settings (below) |  |  |
| Kind | `linking.ramp.kind` | `plunge`, `profile` | `plunge` | How the tool enters the material: straight down (`plunge`), along a zigzag, along a helix, or along the profile. If the chosen ramp does not fit, FluutCAM falls back to a smaller one and warns. Allowed: per type. |
| Angle | `linking.ramp.angle_deg` | degrees | 3 | The angle the tool descends at when it ramps. Allowed: (0, 90]. Depends on: `ramp.kind` ≠ `plunge`. |
| Radius | `linking.ramp.radius` | mm | calculated from 0.5 * tool.diameter | Radius of a helical ramp. Left empty, half the tool diameter. Allowed: > 0. Depends on: `ramp.kind` = `helix`. |
| Order | `linking.order` | `by_level`, `by_area` | `by_level` | `by_level` finishes each depth level over the whole part before going deeper. `by_area` finishes one area through all levels before the next. Depends on: types with levels. |
